_what: Simon's decisions on what the Septimus family site ships, read by scripts/build_site_data.py (docs/technical/septimus-story-filter.md). Policy and per-passage removals/inclusions, each with who decided and when. Gate rulings (G4, G6, the judges) live in decisions.json beside this file.

biblical._ruling: Simon, 2026-11-13: 'I think it makes sense to remove biblical stories so we keep it consistent. I want to find them, but we now exclude from septimus stories and jeff's scholarly work (unless someone filters for them).' After Jeff ruled the Berakhot 54a-b lepers out of scope (R-S1, 2026-11-12). Every story flagged biblical leaves `stories` and is kept in the tractate file's `out_of_scope` list with its reason.

remove._ruling: Jeff's 2026-11-12 not / borderline verdicts on passages the site shipped; the site ships definite stories only (Simon 2026-11-13). Matched by span OVERLAP against the build's own cells (Lesson 36); a removal that matches nothing is named on stderr. The span is the one Jeff was shown (Eruvin: the review card's key, e.g. 53b_8-9 for the site's 53b:8, 67b_15-16 for 67b:15-18). Second batch (Simon 2026-11-14, 'just remove them if you are sure.'): 17 twin-pass cards from unreviewed tractates, flagged while writing summaries and marked SURE_REMOVE by a rules-based triage against docs/STORY_RULES.md; no Jeff verdict on any, so these entries carry no `jeff` field and name their rule and reason (docs/findings/2026-11-14-twin-pass-site-cards.md).

include._ruling: Explicit per-passage inclusions: an expert verdict of `story` plus Simon's yes. The only way past the definite-only filter, and never a rule. Matched by overlap against stories[] of the first run.

passages.decided_by: Jeff Rubenstein 2026-11-12 ('In any case, I would include it'); Simon 2026-11-13 ('Include this')
passages.source: results/shas_run/precision_sample/jeff_verdicts_2026-11-12.json

promote._ruling: A RULE over a graded pool, not a per-passage edit: every passage in `source` (both Claude grader passes said `story` under the judge prompt with sha `judge_prompt_sha`) ships as a story, carrying `included_by` so the whole batch can be filtered or removed in one step. The build refuses if the source file's ids, count or prompt sha differ from this record. Still narrowed by every exclusion (biblical, the judges' not-a-story drop, `remove`, overlap with a story already shipped or out of scope). Model-graded, NOT expert-labelled: never read into a golden, ruler, expert list or recall/precision ruler.

rules.rule: both Claude grader passes say story
rules.evidence: Calibration vs Jeff on 300 spans he ruled: both-passes-story 32/33 = 0.97 precision (Wilson 95% 0.85-1.00), recall 32/141; blind slice 6/6. docs/findings/2026-11-13-low-pool-grader-calibration.md, results/shas_run/low_pool/calibration/score.json

review_bar.planned: Simon reads a seeded random 60 (results/shas_run/low_pool/pool/review_sample.json, validation/ui/low_pool_promotions_review.html); ship only if >= 54 of 60 are yes
review_bar.status: WAIVED / PARTIAL: Simon read part of the sample informally and approved. His per-passage verdicts were not exported, so no count against the 54/60 bar exists.

rules.bounds: the pool unit's cells: the detector span the grade refers to (identical in both runs for 76 of 80; for the other 4 the span of the run that proposed the wider or only one). Not the grader's chosen segments: every other site story is bounded by a detector span, and the grader's picks are relative to a context window and sometimes non-contiguous.
rules.summary: the detector's one_sentence_summary of the SAME passage (identical cells), run 1 then run 2, when reader-facing; otherwise none. Never the grader's reason.
rules.words: Im looking through these stories and they seem to mostly be stories so far. I didnt review all of them, but I suggest we add them at this point.
